records.title: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite with recursive field value structure
Add module extraction functionality with recursive module reference support
records.body:
## Problem Statement
Currently, there is no built-in functionality to extract a Terraform module and all its references (including nested/child modules) from the codebase.

## Desired Functionality
- Add a feature that allows users to extract a specified module from the repository.
- The extraction should include all related module references (local and potentially remote modules).
- Module references should be identified recursively, so if a module calls other modules, those are also included in the extraction process.
- Provide CLI support to invoke this functionality.
- Ensure it is robust for complex module hierarchies.

## Potential Benefits
- Easier refactoring and migration to different repositories or environments
- Improved module maintainability and dependency clarity

## Acceptance Criteria
- CLI command exists to extract a module and its references
- Extracted content includes all nested module dependencies
- Documentation is updated to describe its usage
- Unit/integration tests included for key functionality

## Additional context
Please consider edge cases such as remote and deeply-nested modules.

records.title: Add typed recursive CTE support
records.body:
## Goal

Extend the existing CTE builder with recursive CTEs for hierarchy and graph-style queries.

## Scope

Add `withRecursive` to compose an anchor query with a recursive member using UNION ALL semantics and expose the resulting CTE columns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Valid WITH RECURSIVE SQL is produced for SQLite, MySQL 8+, and PostgreSQL.
- [ ] Anchor and recursive members require compatible projection columns/types.
- [ ] Resulting CTEs work with existing typed select and join support.
- [ ] Tests include a representative hierarchy traversal across all three dialects.
- [ ] Docs state version requirements, recursion limits, and a cycle-safety note.

## Out of scope

Automatic cycle detection and SEARCH/CYCLE clauses.

records.title: Recursive relationships
records.body:
Hi there 👋 

I'm trying to work with recursive relationships.

```
TutorialD (master/main): rec := relation{tuple{src 0, tgt 1}, tuple{src 1, tgt 2}, tuple{src 2, tgt 3}}
TutorialD (master/main): :showexpr rec
┌────────────┬────────────┐
│src::Integer│tgt::Integer│
├────────────┼────────────┤
│0           │1           │
│1           │2           │
│2           │3           │
└────────────┴────────────┘
```

It seems to work ok for a depth 1 traversal:
```
TutorialD (master/main): :showexpr ((rec where src=0) join (rec rename {tgt as tgt2, src as tgt}))
┌────────────┬────────────┬─────────────┐
│src::Integer│tgt::Integer│tgt2::Integer│
├────────────┼────────────┼─────────────┤
│0           │1           │2            │
└────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┘
```

Also if I add an edge:
```
TutorialD (master/main): insert rec relation{tuple{src 1, tgt 4}}
TutorialD (master/main): :showexpr rec
┌────────────┬────────────┐
│src::Integer│tgt::Integer│
├────────────┼────────────┤
│1           │4           │
│2           │3           │
│1           │2           │
│0           │1           │
└────────────┴────────────┘
TutorialD (master/main): :showexpr ((rec where src=0) join (rec rename {tgt as tgt2, src as tgt}))
┌────────────┬────────────┬─────────────┐
│src::Integer│tgt::Integer│tgt2::Integer│
├────────────┼────────────┼─────────────┤
│0           │1           │2            │
│0           │1           │4            │
└────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┘
```

I can work out a way to do a depth 2 traversal:
```
TutorialD (master/main): :showexpr ((rec where src=0) join (rec rename {tgt as tgt2, src as tgt}) join (rec rename {tgt as tgt3, src as tgt2}))
┌────────────┬────────────┬─────────────┬─────────────┐
│src::Integer│tgt::Integer│tgt2::Integer│tgt3::Integer│
├────────────┼────────────┼─────────────┼─────────────┤
│0           │1           │2            │3            │
└────────────┴────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┘
```

Can this be generalised to a depth `n` traversal? Also would it be possible to group the result by depth? 

Thanks for your time!

Jun

records.title: Workspace centre as a root Container — unify with recursive container model
records.body:
The floating workspace centre currently renders frames via `FloatingFrameBackend` directly — it's not wrapped in a Container. Making the workspace centre a root Container with `layout: 'free'` would unify everything:

- Frames become entries in a Container
- Toolbar is the standard container toolbar (no special workspace toolbar)
- Workspace mode switching is just `container.setLayout()`
- Z-order, DnD, snap zones move into the free-layout strategy
- The recursive container model applies root to leaf with no special cases

This is a significant refactor — the backend orchestrates frame lifecycle (z-order, DnD, snap zones) which doesn't map cleanly to the Container model yet. Design discussion needed before implementation.

Builds on #345 (recursive container model), #367 (arrange button), #368 (toolbar position).

records.title: Blank lines in the middle of the query prevents from correct execution
records.body:
### Description

This is valid SQLite query which works through other SQLIte GUI:

```
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS nodes;

CREATE TABLE nodes (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    parent_id INTEGER,
    name TEXT
);

-- 2. Insert sample data (a simple tree structure)
INSERT INTO nodes (id, parent_id, name) VALUES
(1, NULL, 'Root'),
(2, 1, 'Child 1'),
(3, 1, 'Child 2'),
(4, 2, 'Grandchild 1'),
(5, 2, 'Grandchild 2'),
(6, 3, 'Grandchild 3'),
(7, 4, 'Great-Grandchild 1');

-- 3. Recursive CTE to get all descendants of node with id = 2
WITH RECURSIVE subtree AS (
    -- Anchor member: start from the given node
    SELECT id, parent_id, name, 0 as depth
    FROM nodes
    WHERE id = 2  -- Change this ID to get a different subtree

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive member: get children of the current subtree
    SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, n.name, s.depth + 1
    FROM nodes n
    INNER JOIN subtree s ON n.parent_id = s.id
)
SELECT * FROM subtree;
```

DBeaver displays errors for this query:
SQL Error [1]: [SQLITE_ERROR] SQL error or missing database (near ")": syntax error)

DBeaver Version 25.1.0.202506011722

Windows 11

SQLite

2. Open the SQL editor and paste the SQL code shown above
